relevance_note: Case series with individual-level clinical and genetic data on TNFAIP3 carriers: 'Herein, we report eight patients with HA20 from three unrelated families in China.'
method_note: Read the whole paper (no supplementary section present) and built the JSON with a Python script in my scratch directory; every value was chosen from my reading. Table 1 cells were split by script on '|' and checked by eye against the table. Table 1 has no label column; its rows were matched to text-described persons by pedigree number, sex and ages: row 1 = P1 (onset 18, diagnosis 28); rows 2-4 = P1's mother IV:14 and sisters V:22, V:26 (the three rows are identical, so their order is unknown but does not change any value); row 5 = IV:1 of Family 2 (onset 9, diagnosis 12); row 6 = P2 (onset 15, diagnosis 35); row 7 = P3; row 8 = IV:1 of Family 3. Text labels were used instead of 'Table 1 row k'. TABLE SYMBOLS: cells use an en dash '–' while the legend defines '+, postive; -, negative' with a hyphen; I treated the en dash as the legend's negative symbol and quoted the legend as an extra span. 'UN' (unknown) = not reported. LABELS: probands P1, P2, P3 (paper's labels); relatives by pedigree number. Both daughters are 'IV:1' in the paper, so they are disambiguated as 'IV:1 (Family 2)' and 'IV:1 (Family 3)'. The Family 2 cousin 'III:3' is a different person from P3 (pedigree III:3 of Family 3). SCOPE: included P1's father IV:13 (described as having no symptoms; NOD2 variant described as paternal). Excluded: P1's grandmother III:2 and maternal grandfather III:3 (mentioned only as being cousins), cousin V:10 and 'her son' VI:7 (only G6PD deficiency mentioned; whose son is ambiguous). Included untested affected relatives: Family 2 aunt II:3 and cousins III:3, III:4 (they refused gene testing, so no variant rows), Family 3 mother II:4 and late maternal grandmother I:4 (no testing stated). The literature review (126 patients from 35 articles) is group-level only, so it has no rows. CONTRADICTIONS: (1) P1 genital ulcers: text 'She had recurrent oral and genital ulcers from the age of 22' (and Discussion) vs Table 1 row 1 Genital ulcers '–'; both rows emitted, checklist not reported. (2) P2 fever: text 'without recurrent fever' vs Table 1 row 6 Fever '+'; checklist not reported. (3) IV:1 (Family 2) fever: text 'recurrent fever ... since the age of nine' vs Table 1 row 5 Fever '–'; checklist not reported. The Fever cells of rows 5 and 6 look swapped relative to the text. (4) P3 autoantibodies: 'Blood tests for CBC, biochemistry panel, and autoantibodies were all normal' vs positive anti-TG and anti-TPO antibodies in the text and Table 1; both rows emitted, checklist not reported. (5) P3 age at onset: Table 1 gives 15, the text says 'recurrent oral ulcers since the age of 10'; age_at_onset holds the table value 15, and the oral-ulcer feature row holds onset 10. (6) A547T pathogenicity: the abstract says 'validated to be pathogenic' but the Discussion says 'the accurate pathogenic significance of A547T was indeed unknown' (only in-silico modelling, no functional study); both are quoted. (7) P1 arthritis: Table 1 '+' and Discussion say arthritis, but the case text describes 'joint pain ... without joint swelling'; this is not a direct contradiction, and both are recorded. (8) c.1906+2T>G is marked '(exon 7)' in Table 1 but analysed in intron 7 in the text. (9) P3 has Genital ulcers '+' in Table 1 while the text describes only a 'perianal ulcer with an abscess'; recorded per the table. INHERITANCE: left 'not reported' for every TNFAIP3 carrier, because the paper never states inheritance explicitly, even though carrier parents are named (P1's mother for P1 and her sisters; P2 for her daughter; P3 for his daughter). This is recorded in parental_testing_statement. The father's TNFAIP3 genotype appears only in the pedigree figure, which is unavailable. NOD2 is recorded as 'inherited paternal' ('paternal heterozygous'); the father has no NOD2 row because the paper does not attribute it to him directly. Variant type for R271X is 'not reported' (the authors never name the class). CONSANGUINITY: 'the proband’s grandmother (III:2) and maternal grandfather (III:3) were cousins' concerns the grandparents; no one's parents are stated to be consanguineous, so 'not reported'. AGES: the Table 1 'Age at diagnosis' column fills age at diagnosis. The probands' narrative ages (28, 35, 40) equal their diagnosis ages and they were followed up afterwards, so their age at last evaluation is 'not reported'. The daughters' narrative ages ('13-year-old', '10-year-old') are recorded as age at last evaluation. Rows 2-4 give '>18' at diagnosis (no ISO value). CHECKLIST JUDGEMENTS: a normal CBC excludes cytopenia (P1, P3). P2's 'moderate anemia' is not stated to be autoimmune, so cytopenia (autoimmune) is 'not reported'. P1's normal chest CT excludes interstitial lung disease, and her 'no ... vascular disease' excludes vasculitis. P3's Henoch-Schonlein purpura (age 30) counts as vasculitis observed; his Table 1 'Skin lesions –' is kept as excluded, although HSP may imply past purpura. Narrow absences (no arthritis or polyarthritis, no uveitis, no folliculitis, no abdominal pain) did not exclude the composite checklist items. For IV:1 (Family 3), Table 1 'Uveitis –' plus 'without ... ocular symptoms' excluded 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation'. The father IV:13 'had no symptoms' is one excluded feature row; his checklist is left 'not reported'. 'no ... vulva ulcers' excluded genital ulcers for the aunt and both cousins (the cousins' sex is not stated). Post-treatment absence of symptoms was not used as exclusion. ETHNICITY: 'Chinese Han' for the eight HA20 patients; 'Chinese' (from the pedigree title) for the other relatives. HPO IDs are given only where I am confident.
